question: The works on Slovenia’s H4 expressway, which is a natural continuation of Italy’s A34 motorway, will mean severe restrictions and diversions for heavy goods traffic, with significant negative effects on the Gorizia area’s transport and logistics sector, as well as an increase in CO2 emissions.

Gorizia Interport, which is crucial for trade flows between eastern and western Europe, risks suffering permanent economic damage due to the diversion of traffic to other less wellequipped infrastructure, such as Fernetti Interport. These restrictions, expected to last until 2027, could jeopardise the free movement of goods in the European Union and distort the internal market.

In addition, subjecting heavy goods vehicles to diversions and forced stops along alternative routes will lead to an increase in CO2 emissions and have a negative impact on hauliers’ activity. In the light of the above: 1.
Is the Commission aware of the matter described? Has it identified any infringements of the EU legislation in force on the free movement of goods?
What steps will it take to urge Slovenia to ensure the smooth flow of cross-border traffic, given the significant negative impact on Italy’s logistics sector and exports at the moment?
answer: Maintenance works and structural works are needed in particular to ensure sufficient road safety levels on the road infrastructure. Those works can have an impact on traffic which requires the imposition of road traffic restrictions.

Road safety may be considered an overriding reason of public interest that can justify the restriction of free movement as set out in Articles 34 and 35 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union.

The Commission does not have any information at this stage indicating that road traffic restrictions related to Slovenia’s H4 expressway are manifestly discriminatory or inappropriate to the purpose of ensuring the necessary road safety level.
